title: Introduce token-entropy cohorting and observability weft
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Adds token entropy cohort metrics, a new aggregated 'weft' rollup used by dashboards and alert routing; ships an alert-path debouncer and tuned default SLO thresholds for long-tail token noise.
description:
Motivation: We see a lot of noisy alerts driven by long-tail tokenized responses where entropy spikes correlate with higher per-invocation cost and spurious latency variance. Existing rollups treat all invocations the same and sampling misses cohort-specific behavior (e.g., high-entropy prompt families that trigger repeated KV warmups). This PR introduces a lightweight cohorting layer based on token entropy + warmup signal and a new aggregation called 'weft' that fuses entropy, KV-warmup, and queue/backpressure markers. Goals: (1) surface cohort-level cost/latency signal so SREs and product engineers can triage noisy alert groups; (2) reduce alert churn by debouncing alerts at the cohort routing layer; (3) provide a dashboard surface with heatmap + timelines for cohort life-cycle and cost contribution.

What this changes: single continuous change set that touches telemetry ingestion, rollup generator, alerting, dashboards, and SDK tagging.

Checklist: - [x] Add entropy computation and cohort assignment in invocation enrich pipeline - [x] Emit cohort labels to traces and metrics (invocation.cohort, weft.score) - [x] Implement lightweight weft rollup generator and compact timeseries export - [x] New Grafana panels and an exploratory notebook for cohort debugging - [x] Alert-path debouncer: prevents duplicate alert fires across cohorts for the same tenant within 10m window - [x] Unit + integration tests for cohort assignment and rollup correctness - [x] Docs: developer doc describing cohort tuning knobs and recommended thresholds

Commits summary: feat(telemetry): compute token_entropy and kv_warmup flag per invocation; feat(rollup): weft aggregator and cohort timeseries export; perf(ingest): sampling-aware cohort assignment; feat(alerts): path-level debouncer and weighted alert score; docs: cohorting tuning guide + dashboard README; test: add synthetic scenarios and replay tests.

Files touched (high-level): - telemetry/enrich/invocation_enricher.py (compute token_entropy, heuristics for warmup) - telemetry/rollups/weft_aggregator.go (weft score computation, rollup emitters) - observability/alerts/alert_debouncer_service.py (debounce logic + redis-backed window) - dashboards/grafana/cohort_weft_dashboard.json (new dashboard panels + links to notebook) - sdk/annotations/ts/client_tags.ts (expose invocation.cohort tag for SDK users) - tests/integration/test_cohort_rollups.py (replay scenarios)

Small snippets included for reviewer context but diffs are intentionally compact: - We compute token entropy using log-probability distribution over token logits when available; fallback uses shannon-approx from soft-token-scores. - Weft score = weighted sum( normalized_entropy * 0.6, kv_warmup_flag * 0.25, queue_backpressure_score * 0.15 ). Coefficients are configurable via runtime flags keyed by deployment tier.

Review conversation (summary): Diego: \"How deterministic is cohort assignment across retries/coldstarts? We need stable keys so rollups don't fragment.\" Response (Priya): \"Cohort key is derived from hashed(prompt-shape + top-k-entropy-bucket + model_id); stable across retries and stored as invocation attribute in the trace to allow post-hoc joins.\" Marta: \"Will debouncing hide true multi-tenant incidents where multiple cohorts spike?\" Response: \"Debouncer uses tenant-scoped windows and preserves one high-priority fire if sustained beyond 3 samples; docs include recommended tuning for multi-tenant detection.\" Alexei: \"Can we get lightweight cardinality controls?\" Response: \"Added cap: dynamic cohort eviction after 7d inactivity and max 5k cohorts per tenant; metrics exported for evictions so SRE can tune.\"

CI summary: - lint: pass - unit-tests: pass (coverage bump for telemetry) - integration-tests(replay): pass (synthetic scenarios) - e2e(dashboards): pass - perf-smoke: marginal regression on 99th latency in synthetic bench (+2.1%); flagged but acceptable for rollout behind a feature flag.

Rollout plan: - Feature flagged: weft rollup off by default for existing tenants. - Gradual enablement: internal tenants -> beta customers (by request) -> global enable after 30d monitoring. - Observability playbook added to docs/grafana/cohort_weft_readme.md describing how to use the dashboard, investigate cohort spikes, and rollback the flag.

Why this is different from previous work: prior PRs introduced many token-level metrics and span enrichers but treated signals individually. The weft aggregation intentionally fuses multiple signals into a cohort-aware surface so SREs can reason about emergent behavior (entropy + warmup + queueing) rather than chasing isolated metric spikes. The alert-path debouncer is conservative and tenant-aware to reduce churn without masking true incidents.

Post-merge actions: - Enable feature flag for internal staging on 2026-03-02 - Run 2-week smoke on internal traffic and monitor weft_eviction_count, cohort_count_per_tenant, and debouncer_suppressed_fires - Follow-up PR to add adaptive coefficient autotune (ENG-1302) in the rollup generator.
